dataset.source: MoSPI Quarterly Progress Information System Reports (QPISR) and Flash Reports (public data), parsed from official PDFs

split_policy.description: Time-aware splits: earlier report months train, middle months validate (threshold & calibration selection), the most recent month is held out for testing. Project-month rows use only information available at that month (see leakage notes).
leakage_notes: Excluded as features: revised cost, anticipated cost, latest cost, cost-overrun %, time overrun, cost-overrun flag, actual/revised completion dates, physical progress-linked outcome fields.
These fields define the prediction targets; using them as inputs would leak the outcome into the model.
Monitoring-stage features use only information accumulated up to the report month (age, elapsed schedule fraction, expenditure pattern).
Validation is time-based: earlier report months train, later months validate, the most recent month is held out for testing.

state: State where the project is located
log_original_cost: log( original approved cost in Rs crore )
expenditure_over_original_pct: (Cumulative expenditure - original cost) / original cost x 100, as known at the report month
report_month_idx: Report month as a numeric index

classification_approval_stage.flag_definition: cost_overrun_flag = 1 when the current (revised/anticipated) cost exceeds the original approved cost - consistent with MoSPI flash-report counting.

project_disjoint.description: Entire projects held out (train 60% / val 15% / test 25% of project codes) - measures generalisation to projects never seen during training. The primary time-split metrics above share projects across months (panel data), which inflates scores by partially recognising the same project.

classification_monitoring_stage.flag_definition: cost_overrun_flag = 1 when the current (revised/anticipated) cost exceeds the original approved cost - consistent with MoSPI flash-report counting.

survival_time_overrun.reason: Survival models achieved cross-validated concordance <= 0.55 - no better than chance - so regression on reported schedule delay is used instead.

feasibility.note: Per-project ARIMA/ETS forecasting requires at least 12 monthly observations per project; the panel provides at most 6. PAIMANA therefore uses a global panel model with lag features (evaluated against a naive baseline) until longer series are available.

forecast_cost_overrun_pct.note: Global panel model (CatBoost with lag features). The naive baseline predicts next month = current month; the panel model is used only where it beats the baseline on the hold-out month.

anomaly_detection.method: Isolation Forest (3% contamination) on scaled cost/schedule/expenditure indicators of the latest report month per project.

similarity_benchmarking.features: sector + ministry + state (one-hot), log original cost, planned duration (scaled)
similarity_benchmarking.method: k-NN (k=10 peers) in standardized feature space

classification_approval.metric_note: Models compared on the same time-based test split (most recent report month); comparison computed from the actual dataset.

classification_monitoring.metric_note: Models compared on the same time-based test split (most recent report month); comparison computed from the actual dataset.

risk_score.components: cost_risk, schedule_risk, expenditure_risk, reporting_risk - each a documented formula (see /api/risk/methodology or the Risk Methodology page)

shap_global.caveat: SHAP values show how strongly each feature influenced the model's prediction for this project. They are associations learned from historical data, not causal effects.

future_variables: Contractor / implementing-agency identity and past performance
Detailed structured delay reasons (currently only headline categories from flash-report tables)
Sanctioned vs released funds and sanction-to-award lag
Land acquisition and statutory clearance milestone dates
Physical milestone completion (currently only cumulative % progress)
future_variables_note: These variables are NOT present in the current public MoSPI extracts. They are recommended future PAIMANA collections.
